verdict.justification: Both deliverables follow the requested nine-slide structure and report the key cumulative spend figures and risk ratings consistently with the supplied material. B is more useful for an assessor because its spend slide separates the individual cost lines and explains how personnel, stationery and travel contribute to the £424.33 variance, whereas A groups several of those costs together. More importantly, B explicitly identifies the conflict between the 7 November submission and incorporation of stakeholder comments on 9 November, offering a clearly labelled proposal for agreement rather than merely repeating both dates as A does. B also turns current focus into an actionable table with owners, deadlines and statuses, and flags that the SpinBits trial licence is not confirmed in the log. A introduces a clear reporting-date error by saying that the 3 November spend review 'was held' in a report dated 30 October. B is not flawless: its statement that the architecture was 'acceptance-tested on 15 Oct' is stronger than the log's evidence of planned testing and subsequent feedback, and its slides are more text-heavy. Nevertheless, its stronger reconciliation of source inconsistencies and more decision-oriented auditor questions make it the preferable professional deliverable.
